summary: A phase signal in status "running" with a live worker is re-claimed roughly every two minutes (10 claims in ~30 min for CTL-2128 phase-plan on mini, 2026-08-22), and each re-claim leaves the prior generation as an orphan (ppid 1) that outlives its generation by up to ~14 minutes. The re-dispatcher is UNIDENTIFIED — the ticket eliminates three candidates with traces (daemon restarts, the CTL-2110 reclaim crash, duplicate-dispatch storm) and directs the search at the resume sweep and the claim path (whatever writes <phase>.claim.N). Four ACs: stop re-claiming a live running worker (AC1), keep recovering a genuinely dead one (AC2 — the negative control and the hard half), reap the prior generation instead of letting it age out (AC3), and prove it against a captured live signal rather than an authored fixture (AC4).
